sources.cite: International Soling Association, Soling Guide 1992–1995, 'Soling Class Measurement Diagram' (PDF pp. 12–14)
sources.note: The diagram is schematic (local scales 4.03–4.29 mm/px) and never prints the stem-to-BMP distance. Read off it: the keel's straight leading edge produced to the hull 0.333 m aft of the BMP, the trailing edge 1.365 m aft of it; chord 1.03 m at the hull, 1.09 at the base; span 0.96 (1.00 max given); sweep 34.6° ± 2°. The dimensioned 3470 is reconstructed from the readings to 2 mm; other checks are within 3–5%, so the keel's position carries ±0.06 m. Closing the diagram's own dimensions puts the BMP 2.98 ± 0.04 m aft of the stem; ORC's SFJ puts it at 0.490 + 2.320 = 2.810 m.

polar.note: ORC rates downwind with the spinnaker (36.38 m²); the VPP has none, so only the beat and 52–90° are compared.

mastAftOfStem.how: ORC's SFJ 0.490 plus J 2.650. By the class rule the mast is 0.27 ± 0.05 m aft of the BMP and the forestay 2.320 forward of it, J 2.590 ± 0.055: ORC's J is at the top of that tolerance

keelLeAftOfStem.how: 0.333 m aft of the BMP on the class measurement diagram, the BMP 2.810 m aft of the stem by ORC's SFJ and the rule's 2320 mm

balance.why: Every rig dimension is a class rule or an ORC measurement, and mast, forestay and keel share one datum (the BMP), so the stem's uncertain place doesn't enter the lead. The keel's edges are read off a schematic diagram (±0.06 m), and ORC's J is 0.06 m longer than the rule's nominal.

disagreements.effect: with the rule's nominal the mast is 0.06 m further forward: the lead 1.0% of LWL more

published.estimatedWhy: BWL is solved from ORC's sink; Tc is ORC's draft less the diagram's keel span. The keel's planform and sweep are read off the class diagram; its section is the one that makes 580 kg of cast iron. The rudder's chords are the rule diagram's; its span (0.81–0.85 m normal to the top edge), sweep and position along the hull are worked from the rule's quadrilateral and a counter slope read off the diagram. The crew's weight is the middle of ORC's range.
